instruction: Open /home/user/Desktop/multi_feature.step and /home/user/Desktop/tool_library.csv in FreeCAD Path/CAM. The STEP is the finished 120 x 80 x 18 mm part at X=-60..60, Y=-40..40, Z=0..18. It has a centered 50 x 30 x 6 mm top pocket with R8 inside corners, two through holes of diameter 14 mm at (-42, 0) and (42, 0), and two through holes of diameter 12 mm at (0, -28) and (0, 28). Use the CSV as the tool-definition table and create native FreeCAD ToolBits and Tool Controllers exactly as listed; do not use any tool outside it. Use T1, the diameter-16 end mill, for milling; T2, the diameter-14 118-degree drill, for the diameter-14 holes; and T3, the diameter-12 118-degree drill, for the diameter-12 holes. Set all three controllers to forward spindle S7000 and horizontal/vertical feed 500 mm/min. Create one native Path Job with G54 at the finished part's top-face center, so the Job model spans X=-60..60, Y=-40..40, Z=-18..0. Define stock with 2 mm extension on every X/Y side, 1 mm above the part, and no bottom extension (X=-62..62, Y=-42..42, Z=-18..1). Create exactly five active native operations in this order: (1) Face with T1 from stock top Z=1 to finished top Z=0 and cover the entire stock top; (2) Pocket with T1 that clears the complete R8 pocket to Z=-6 without gouging outside it; (3) Drilling with T2 for both diameter-14 holes; (4) Drilling with T3 for both diameter-12 holes; and (5) an outside compensated Profile with T1 that follows the complete outer boundary to Z=-18 without entering the finished part. For both Drilling operations use nominal FinalDepth Z=-19, positive safe/retract heights, a safe retract mode, and FreeCAD's Drill Tip extra-offset so the full hole diameter passes 1 mm below the part bottom. Use the FreeCAD 0.21.2 LinuxCNC postprocessor and preserve operation order. Save the editable native Job and the posted program to exactly /home/user/Desktop/task-05.FCStd and /home/user/Desktop/task-05.nc. [Software] To use FreeCAD, run `freecad` from a terminal (use the full executable path if it is not on PATH). For the steps below, use `/usr/lib/freecad/bin/freecadcmd-python3` for FreeCAD Path command-line automation when working on `multi_feature.step`.
